blocks.title: Rules for a good drawing
blocks.md:
1. Use a sharp **HB pencil** and a clean eraser; draw on plain paper.
2. Make the drawing **large**, using more than half of the space.
3. Draw with **clear, continuous lines**; no shading, no colouring (unless asked), no sketching.
4. Show only what you can see; keep **proportions** correct.
5. **Label** with ruled straight lines that touch the structure and never cross; write labels in pencil, horizontally.
6. Give a **title** and state the **magnification** or add a **scale bar**.

blocks.caption: A labelled drawing with title and scale bar (schematic).
blocks.alt: A green rounded cell with a yellow nucleus; three leader lines labelled cell wall, nucleus and cytoplasm; a title Fig. 1 a plant cell and a scale bar of 10 micrometres.

blocks.title: Magnification
blocks.md:
**Magnification = size of the image ÷ actual size** (measure in the same units).

Actual size = image size ÷ magnification. Image size = actual size × magnification.

Units: **1 mm = 1000 µm** (micrometres); 1 cm = 10 mm. A magnification has no units (×400).

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Do not mix units: convert both lengths to the same unit first.
- Do not draw cells with thick double lines or shade them.
- Label lines must never cross each other or end with arrows.
- Do not copy the textbook; draw what *you* see.

blocks.title: Variables
blocks.md:
In an experiment you change one factor and measure another.

- **Independent variable**: the one you change on purpose.
- **Dependent variable**: the one you measure.
- **Controlled variables**: everything else, kept the same so the test is **fair**.

A **control** experiment lacks the factor being tested, to show that it is the factor that causes the result.

blocks.title: Tables and graphs
blocks.md:
**Table**: the independent variable in the first column, with **headings and units**; repeat the measurements and calculate the **mean**.

**Graph**: independent variable on the **x-axis**, dependent on the **y-axis**; label both axes with units; choose an even scale that uses most of the paper; plot points as small crosses; draw a smooth curve or **line of best fit**; give a title.

blocks.caption: Cumulative volume of gas against time (illustrative).
blocks.alt: A graph of five red points that lie close to a straight line from the origin rising about 2 units per minute.

blocks.title: Writing a plan
blocks.md: State: the **aim**; the **apparatus**; the **method** step by step (what to change, measure and keep constant, how many repeats); what to **record**; how to **process** the results (mean, rate, graph); **safety** precautions. Evaluate: **reliability** (repeat and agree), **anomalous results**, sources of error, improvements.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Changing two factors at once makes the test unfair.
- Forgetting units on table headings and graph axes.
- Joining points dot-to-dot instead of drawing a best-fit line when the points are scattered.
- Taking a conclusion that the data do not support.

blocks.title: Calculate a rate from a graph
blocks.statement: On the graph, gas production is 2.0 bubbles at 1 min and 10.0 bubbles at 5 min. Calculate the average rate.
steps: Change in time = 5 − 1 = 4 min; rate = 8 ÷ 4 = 2 bubbles per minute.

blocks.title: Name the variables
blocks.statement: A student investigates how temperature affects the rate of bubbling of yeast in sugar solution. Name the independent, dependent and two controlled variables.
steps: Dependent: number of bubbles per minute; controlled: mass of yeast, volume and concentration of sugar solution, time.
blocks.answer: Independent: temperature; dependent: bubbles per minute; controlled: yeast mass and sugar concentration
